correctness.rationale: For every geometric critical point, the deletion identity forces all coordinates to be roots of a common monic quadratic. The two-value equation (D_i+D_j)=(x_i+x_j)sum_{l not i,j}x_l and parity of the block sizes force precisely the nonzero supports of size 1 mod 4 when n is not 2 mod 4. Localizing at each point and inverting cross-block differences forces all coordinates equal within each block as scheme equations: the remaining affine-chart algebra is k for odd n and k[b]/(b^2) for 4|n. The projective Hessian polar form has full rank for odd n; for 4|n its one-dimensional radical has nonzero quadratic value, proving a smooth projectivized tangent cone. Euler equality makes the gradient scheme the hypersurface singular scheme. A roots-of-unity filter gives the exact node count and all local lengths. Standalone F2 and F4 enumeration and GF2 Hessian rank checks agree for the specified finite ranges; these do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the smaller-dimensional critical locus explicitly left unresolved in the motivating full-text paper, for the first degree where the two-value constraint is nontrivial. It determines an exponentially growing count of hypersurface ordinary nodes together with a characteristic-two scheme-theoretic dichotomy: reduced Jacobian points for odd n versus a length-two local Artin algebra at every node for 4|n. The distinction clarifies why a smooth quadratic tangent cone need not make the Jacobian scheme reduced in characteristic two and supplies an exact finite geometric invariant, not an arbitrary isolated numerical case.
